Comorbidity indicators

Source: vignettes/articles/comorbidity.Rmd
comorbidity.Rmd

nis_comorbidity() scores secondary diagnoses within each discharge in DuckDB. For a lazy input, it checks the discharge keys and code availability and returns a query. The flags and indices are calculated when that query runs.

Choose a definition

method Coding definition and published weights
elixhauser_ahrq_icd10 (default) Union of AHRQ Refined ICD-10-CM FY2022–FY2026 codes and the latest weights in medicalcoder 0.10.0.
elixhauser_ahrq2022 through elixhauser_ahrq2026 Pinned AHRQ Refined ICD-10-CM definitions and their in-hospital mortality and 30-day readmission weights, supplied by medicalcoder.
elixhauser_ahrq2027 AHRQ Refined ICD-10-CM v2027.1. Exemptions are selected by discharge fiscal year when available.
charlson_quan2005 Quan 2005 ICD-9-CM and ICD-10 coding with the original Charlson weights.
charlson_quan2011 Quan 2005 ICD-9-CM and ICD-10 coding with Quan 2011 weights.
charlson_deyo1992 Deyo 1992 ICD-9-CM coding with the original Charlson weights. Eligible ICD-9-CM procedure slots are used when supplied.
elixhauser_quan2005 Quan 2005 ICD-9-CM and ICD-10 Elixhauser coding with legacy AHRQ index weights, as supplied by medicalcoder.
elixhauser_ahrq_web, elixhauser_elixhauser1998 Legacy ICD-9-CM code mappings and AHRQ index weights, as supplied by medicalcoder. The scorer uses diagnosis codes without diagnosis-related group exclusions.

The Charlson score is unadjusted for age. For the scientific definitions, see Charlson et al. (1987), Deyo et al. (1992), Elixhauser et al. (1998), Quan et al. (2005), Quan et al. (2011), Moore et al. (2017), and the AHRQ Refined software and user guide.

Methods other than FY2027 use mappings from medicalcoder. Install it with install.packages("medicalcoder"). It remains an optional dependency so workflows that do not use those definitions avoid the extra download, about 3.3 MB for the 0.10.0 source archive. CRAN publishes Windows and macOS binaries. CRAN’s Linux source package needs no compilation and has no additional mandatory package dependencies.

Score a lazy cohort 

discharges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 18) |>
  dplyr::mutate(KEY_NIS = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::compute()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dciqv/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dciqv/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
scored <- nis_comorbidity(discharges, method = "elixhauser_ahrq2027")
#> Warning: No matching POA column for 40 diagnosis slots: I10_DX1, I10_DX10, I10_DX11,
#> I10_DX12, I10_DX13, I10_DX14, I10_DX15, I10_DX16, I10_DX17, I10_DX18, I10_DX19,
#> I10_DX2, I10_DX20, I10_DX21, I10_DX22, I10_DX23, I10_DX24, I10_DX25, I10_DX26,
#> I10_DX27, I10_DX28, I10_DX29, I10_DX3, I10_DX30, I10_DX31, I10_DX32, I10_DX33,
#> I10_DX34, I10_DX35, I10_DX36, I10_DX37, I10_DX38, I10_DX39, I10_DX4, I10_DX40,
#> I10_DX5, I10_DX6, I10_DX7, I10_DX8, I10_DX9. Assuming present.
#> ℹ POA-dependent comorbidities may include conditions acquired in hospital.
scored |>
  dplyr::select(AGE, cmrb_n, cmrb_any, cmrb_mortality_index) |>
  head() |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>     AGE cmrb_n cmrb_any cmrb_mortality_index
#>   <dbl>  <int> <lgl>                   <int>
#> 1    28      1 TRUE                       14
#> 2    35      1 TRUE                        0
#> 3    42      1 TRUE                        0
#> 4    49      0 FALSE                       0
#> 5    56      1 TRUE                       14
#> 6    63      1 TRUE                        0

The example assigns keys to the invented fixture. NIS files supply KEY_NIS. When pooling years, keep YEAR because keys can repeat across years. Keep eligible DX* and I10_DX* slots plus YEAR, DQTR, and DXVER where available when scoring data across the October 2015 transition. The selected method determines which coding systems are eligible.

Score a survey design

Keep diagnosis and available POA columns in the design to add the indicators after constructing it. Weights, strata and clusters are preserved.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dciqv/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3dciqv/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure,
  keep = c(AGE, dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX"), dplyr::starts_with("DXPOA"))
)
#> Cohort: 54 discharges; weighted N 62.4; 9 hospitals across 1 years.
scored_design <- nis_comorbidity(design, method = "elixhauser_ahrq2027")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Warning: No matching POA column for 40 diagnosis slots: I10_DX1, I10_DX10, I10_DX11,
#> I10_DX12, I10_DX13, I10_DX14, I10_DX15, I10_DX16, I10_DX17, I10_DX18, I10_DX19,

#> I10_DX5, I10_DX6, I10_DX7, I10_DX8, I10_DX9. Assuming present.

head(scored_design$variables[c("AGE", "cmrb_n", "cmrb_any")])

#>     AGE cmrb_n cmrb_any

Interpret missing values

A record with a usable code and zero mapped conditions gets zero scores. A discharge without a usable code for the selected definition gets missing scores. Keep the original ICD-9-CM codes as strings so that leading zeros survive.

For refined Elixhauser and Charlson, Y and W count as present on admission, N and U mean absent, and other values including 1 are unknown. Refined Elixhauser uses its code-level exemptions. The medicalcoder-based releases use its fixed exemption mapping. FY2027 uses YEAR plus one for October through December, the calendar year if the quarter is missing, or the latest available exemption list if the year is missing or beyond that release.

If a matching POA column is absent, easyNIS assumes the corresponding diagnoses were present and warns which slots are affected. The assumption can include conditions acquired during a hospital stay. AHRQ leaves 18 refined measures unset when POA is unavailable, and intends its indices to use all 38 measures. Report the assumption and method when publishing results.

NIS studies may carry Stata-derived ynel* and elixsum columns. They use earlier definitions, so their values may differ from these scores.

See the function reference and Data notes by year.
